sub_questions: How should an adversarial code-review workflow work where one frontier model generates code and a different frontier model critiques it to invalidate bad tests and reject slop?
How should automated benchmarking/eval loops be structured to gate human review?
How should code blast-radius be identified and surfaced before merge?
How can human SOPs be mapped into modular, callable agent Skills (e.g., git rebasing, DB optimization, deep web scraping)?
How can a system analyze a developer's agent-trace history to probabilistically predict and auto-chain skill sequences?
What strategies let agents deep-scan network calls, decompile unknown structures, and auto-map dependencies in legacy/unknown codebases?
How should a scheduled (~90 min) automated penetration-testing / vulnerability-sweep loop be designed, including auto-flag and auto-patch?
How should agents autonomously scan docs/ folders and ADRs, then enforce those architectural rules on newly generated code?
How should context be isolated to relevant workspace trees to prevent context-window bloat?
What event-driven triggers (webhooks, cron schedules, DB connection spikes, customer bug reports) can replace human-typed prompts as the system's activation source?
How should isolated, scalable cloud sandboxes be architected so a Director Agent can spin up 100+ Worker Agents each in its own VM without CPU starvation or conflicts?
What are the token/cost economics of routing heavy agentic workloads through flat-rate consumer subscriptions (via automation/harnesses) versus per-token API pricing?
How should idle/clean-result agents self-archive and self-terminate without paging a human?

levers.domain_notes: Sourcing: current multi-agent orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen/AG2, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, MCP), eval/observability tooling (promptfoo, DeepEval, Braintrust, LangSmith, OpenAI Evals), static/security scanning (Semgrep, CodeQL, Snyk, OWASP ZAP, Trivy), cloud agent-sandbox providers (E2B, Modal, Fly Machines, Daytona, Northflank, Kubernetes-based isolation). Prefer sources within the last 12-18 months given how fast agent tooling moves; engineering blogs, vendor docs, GitHub repos, and arXiv multi-agent-systems papers all count as primary for this domain. Measured benchmark numbers and documented production architectures outrank marketing claims.
